doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Memories of Milt Hinton
summary: Playing with Hinton, who quieted chatter on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well I think it was well said, your thoughts anyway. Everyone has particular memories of Milt Hinton. Do you have any specific things?

Well I first played with him and back then we did some recording for Grand Award, the Command label with Pee Wee Irwin. And then I didn’t see him for a while and then I started growing with him in the circuit. I’ll never forget one time we were playing a particular set and sometimes there’s a little too much chatter on the bandstand. And I was playing and all of a sudden I hear, “Shh.” I look up, I was playing a solo at this time and there were two guys chatting over there. And they looked up and I looked up too, I’m saying what the hell is going on? And he says, “The man’s playing, be quiet.” And you heard silence from that point on. So that’s one of the great memories I have from Milt. I appreciated that so much.

Yeah. He was, the little bit I got to know him I was amazed by just what you pegged there, that he was the greatest man, he was always happy, he was always — but there was a point where he is business. You know, this is a business.
And give it the respect it’s due.
Yeah. Have fun but this is a business. Yeah he was one of a kind, man. I really loved him.
